messages:
alex: FYI I hit a weird case in python-sdk where a 200 comes back with an error body and we raise GenericSDKError. Customer can't tell if it's auth or rate-limit.
mira: Oof. Does the server set any error headers (x-rw-error-code)?
alex: sometimes yes. Example body: {"error": {"type": "rate_limit", "message": "Too many requests"}} but status is 200.
sam: That explains it. Our clients use HTTP status as source-of-truth. Proposal: canonical precedence = header -> body -> status.
lindsey: Also we should expose typed exceptions across SDKs: AuthError, RateLimitError, BadRequestError, ServiceUnavailableError. Make a RetryableError base for transient ones.
mira: Strong +1. Keep top-level messages friendly and put machine codes in err.code/metadata. No raw internal ids in message copy.
alex: Spec draft: if x-rw-error-code header -> map to typed error; else if body.error.type -> map by body.type; else map from HTTP status. Importantly treat 200+error-body as an error.
sam: SDKs should surface should_retry (bool) and retry_after (seconds) when present. Built-in retryers should respect those fields.
mira: Suggest Response.to_error() helper returning typed object with fields: code, category, retryable, hint. Example: err = resp.to_error(); if isinstance(err, RateLimitError) and err.retry_after: sleep(err.retry_after)
lindsey: Mapping table idea: 429 -> RateLimitError (retryable true), 401/403 -> AuthError (retryable false), 400 -> BadRequestError (retryable false), 5xx -> ServiceUnavailableError (retryable true). Special-case 200+body.error.type -> body mapping.
mira: We also need parity tests across languages (JS currently prefers body-first, py prefers status-first). Create a conformance test suite.
dev-bot: Created ticket INF-2345 (error mapping spec) and linked draft PR #4567.
alex: I'll draft the spec + python PR and add a quickstart snippet showing how to handle typed errors. Want to pair on JS parity tomorrow @sam?
sam: 10am PT works. Also let's add a tiny sample app branch demonstrating best-practice handling + retry helpers for onboarding. :thumbsup:
